contradictions.detail: The listing says 'Price includes fees', but the dealer disclaimer says the price 'may exclude taxes, license and title fees and documentary service fee'. An itemised out-the-door figure is needed.

critical_evidence.evidence: CARFAX shows only four service entries in ten years, with reported gaps of about 4 years (2018-2022) and about 3.4 years (2022-2025). No brake fluid flush is reported anywhere. The 10/2026 PDI line 'brakes serviced' does not specify fluid. Oil is documented only at 10/2026. No reported entry is not proof of neglect; owner receipts may exist.

The car is a June 2016 build, inside the early ND1 6MT risk window. CARFAX shows no transmission repair or warranty entry, and there are no Mazda-dealer visits at all. No door-jamb build-label photo was examined here.
Interior photos show clean tan seats and dash. No photos of lifted footwell carpet, seat-rail bolts or the drain area behind the seats were examined here.

CARFAX states 'No open recalls reported to CARFAX', but the detailed history shows no Mazda-dealer recall entries. Two campaigns apply to this manual 2016 car: 19V496000 (skid plate) and 24V695000 (airbag control module software). 19V072000 covers automatics only and does not apply. An NHTSA or Mazda VIN lookup is needed.

CARFAX shows 'Battery replaced' at the selling dealer's PDI on 10/16/2026 and 'Tire(s) replaced' at Car-X on 04/11/2022. The listing makes no 'new tires' claim. Tire DOT date codes were not photographed; confirm they are about 2022.

documentation.rationale: Identity is strong: the VIN matches the decode, and a full CARFAX shows one owner, a guaranteed clean title and a consistent odometer trail. Maintenance evidence is thin: four service entries in ten years with multi-year gaps, no brake fluid or other time-based fluid record, and no transmission or recall documentation. Price terms are ambiguous about fees.

condition.rationale: Photos show a clean, straight car with tidy tan leather and unmarked factory wheels. A fresh battery and oil change are documented. There is no PPI, no underside or engine-bay photo, no running-cluster photo, and ten-year-old fluids are undocumented. Nothing wrong is observed.

price_value.rationale: $21,818 sits near the top of the $18,139-$22,094 fair band, about 10% over the $19,889 midpoint. CARFAX itself rates it $1,238 over its value. The 2016 build year carries the early-gearbox discount factor. No known-work items pull it down further.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual, reliable, simple roadster under the $27,000 ceiling and easy to resell in 6-24 months. Asking is above the $19,000 ideal band, and the early-2016 6MT is the main reliability question for a bridge car.

logistics.rationale: Champaign, IL is a long fly-and-drive from Carmel. A dealer in a college town should allow an independent PPI, but access is not stated. CA registration via smog should be feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: This is a stock one-owner Grand Touring manual in dark gray over tan, a pleasant but typical spec. It is not a Club/Brembo or ND2, and it has the lower-output ND1 engine.

what_would_change_verdict: Up: owner receipts filling the 2018-2025 gaps, especially brake fluid, plus a clean independent PPI with a quiet, crisp-shifting warm gearbox and a dry underside.
Up: a negotiated out-the-door price closer to the $19,889 fair-value midpoint.
Down: grinding or pop-out in 2nd/3rd, clutch slip, or evidence of a gearbox fault at PPI.
Down: significant underbody corrosion, cabin water damage, or a dealer refusal of an independent PPI.
Down: open airbag or skid-plate recalls the dealer will not close before sale.
evidence.mission_note: A stock, one-owner manual MX-5 fits the enthusiast-bridge brief well: simple, reliable, Highway 1-appropriate and easy to resell in 6-24 months. Its early-2016 gearbox and asking price above the ideal band are the points to settle before the long trip from Illinois.
evidence.rationale: The CARFAX establishes a strong identity record: a VIN that matches the decode, one personal owner for ten years in Illinois, a guaranteed clean title, no reported accidents, and a consistent odometer trail ending at 34,462 miles, which the cluster photo confirms. Maintenance evidence is thin. There are only four reported service entries, with gaps of about four and about three years, no reported brake fluid, coolant or gearbox/diff fluid work, and no Mazda-dealer visits. The selling dealer's PDI documents a new battery, oil change and an unspecified brake service, and tires were replaced in 2022. The photos show a straight, stock car with tidy tan leather, but no underside, engine-bay, carpet-lifted or running-cluster views were examined. The June 2016 build date puts the 6MT in the early ND1 risk window, with no transmission history on record. Recall closure for the skid-plate and airbag-software campaigns is not demonstrated by any dated entry. At $21,818, the price sits near the top of the $18,139-$22,094 fair band, and fee inclusion is stated inconsistently.
evidence.next_action: Call Sam Leman to request an itemised out-the-door price, written permission for an independent PPI in Champaign, and photos of the door-jamb build label, tire DOT codes, lifted footwell carpets, top drains and underside.
